claims_boundary: Worldshepherd 10:1, 40:1, 400:1, and >=4000 nautical mile values are design targets, not demonstrated capabilities.
The >=4000 nautical mile range target is a Worldshepherd mission requirement, not a DARPA Lift Challenge requirement.
No empirical Worldshepherd flight or prototype evidence exceeding 4:1 is established by this fixture.
DARPA's 2028 ratio target is not yet published; do not invent it.
Challenge and long-range variants may require different aircraft architectures and must not be silently conflated.

darpa_2026_baseline.interpretation: A 9.63:1 ratio was physically attempted but not completed as an official scored run; a Worldshepherd 10:1 target must therefore be judged on completion, repeatability, control, and mission performance rather than ratio alone.

darpa_dp2_capture_gate.proof_of_concept_requirement: Existing empirical data, flight logs, or prototype test results proving baseline capability at or above 4:1 payload-to-weight, plus first-order analysis.
darpa_dp2_capture_gate.reason: Conceptual design targets and software assurance do not satisfy a DP2 working-proof-of-concept requirement.

mandatory_first_tests: Mass budget including energy source, propulsion, structure, controls, communications, landing gear, and safety systems.
Energy and propulsive-efficiency lower-bound analysis for hover, transition, cruise, reserve, and landing.
Compare multirotor-only, compound/wingborne, tilt/transition, hybrid-electric, turbine, fuel-cell, and other conventional momentum-conserving architectures.
Reject any architecture whose required stored or supplied energy, structure, thermal load, or stability margin violates the declared mass budget.
Keep 4000-nm mission optimization separate from the 10-nm DARPA challenge optimization until a common feasible architecture is demonstrated.

validation_ladder: V0: analytic mass, momentum, energy, thermal, structural, stability, and control bounds
V1: component bench evidence with calibrated uncertainty
V2: subscale tethered and untethered lift tests
V3: repeatable loaded hover and maneuver tests
V4: completed mission-course demonstration with calibrated pre/post weights and logged telemetry
V5: manufacturing repeatability across at least three articles
V6: environmental/endurance testing and failure analysis
near_term_decisions: Do not submit Worldshepherd as a DP2 prime absent existing >=4:1 empirical proof-of-concept evidence.
Screen DefendTex first for high-ratio aerodynamic/structural teaming because DARPA records the 9.63:1 attempted result, while independently verifying availability and fit before any outreach.
Use the 2028 challenge as the principal physical-validation runway for a Worldshepherd-owned 10:1+ aircraft concept.
Treat 40:1 and 400:1 as successive research gates that cannot inherit readiness from the 10:1 vehicle.
Run the >=4000-nm requirement through a separate long-range architecture trade before requiring one vehicle to satisfy both extreme lift ratio and extreme range.
